data.long_meaning: The name Joannis is derived from the Greek name Ioannes, which is composed of the elements 'Iōannēs' (Ioannes) or 'Iōannē' (Ioanna), meaning 'God is gracious'. In the New Testament, the name Ioannes is the Greek form of the Hebrew name Yohanan or the Latin name Johannes. The name was borne by several important figures in Christian history, including St. John the Baptist and St. John the Evangelist, who were central figures in the early Christian community and authors of significant New Testament writings.

The name bears the legacy of two significant figures in the New Testament: St. John the Baptist and St. John the Evangelist. St. John the Evangelist, also known as John of Patmos, was one of the twelve apostles and the author of the fourth gospel and the Revelation of John. Both St. Johns have left an indelible mark on Christianity through their teachings and writings, and the name Joannis continues to evoke their legacies.
